title: BlueSky Social Has Arrived, and it is Prescription Strength Awesome: Jake Tapper of CNN Reporting.
subtitle: Shitposters built the hate-contained future of social media with memes, AI Ducks, and inclusive humor.
body_html:
This article describes the future-that-is-now of hate-mitigated social media. There will be profanity. You have been warned:

A video was posted on the social media site Twitter today.

In that video, reporter Jake Tapper (@jaketapper.bsky.social) reports on a comment made on another social media site, the nascent BlueSky Social.

“On it, Senator Brian Schatz, just Skeeted…(the news in question) ”That is Brian Schatz Skeeting on Blue Sky.”

—Jake Tapper.

I know you want to check that thing and see. The sad state of the world is, you probably can’t.

It’s an invite-only private beta.1

The absurd experiences of nerdy + queer + trans + POC + tech + joyful + absurd users on BlueSky Social is powerful. We are sharing trans women's boobs, AI duck interactions, and controversial jokes. Jake Tapper's comment turned a joke into a social reality. Blue Sky Social is similar to Twitter but decentralized. No single controlling authority runs the show. AOC is throwing down already.2

AOC is talking about right-wing harassment. Because she's a left-wing politician and that's her job. My job, as a physician, is to point out that all harassment function similarly. And all of it is bad. Harassment and humor are opposites, and accountability is part of what BlueSky has solved for early…

The founders have been very public about the details, and some are technical:

We started with a research-intensive process to learn what can be applied from existing decentralized protocols. This research began with the ecosystem review and has continued while the Bluesky team was forming. We will be publishing our preliminary work and research this month, starting with this high level introduction. There are many projects that have created protocols for decentralizing discourse, including ActivityPub and SSB for social, Matrix and IRC for chat, and RSS for blogging. While each of these are successful in their own right, none of them fully met the goals we had for a network that enables global long-term public conversations at scale.

No one human decided that the term should be skeet3. On the bird app, the analogous action is referred to as a tweet. Leadership thought this action would be called posts. The culture of shitposting absurdists? Well, we thought differently:

Shitposting (noun)

Vulgar Slang.

The activity of posting deliberately provocative or off-topic comments on social media, typically to upset others or distract from the main conversation.

Shitposting has a fundamentally prosocial connotation:

Greszes compared shitposting to Dadaism's "confusing, context-free pieces that, specifically because they were so absurd, were seen as revolutionary works both artistically and politically.” The goal of shitposting is "to make an audience so confused at the lack of content that they laugh4 or smile.”

A goddamn CNN reporter just decided to take absurd humor and report that as news. Which makes it true. Sup, . And sup .

We get to make meaningful decisions:

  • Anyone can define and apply “labels” to content or accounts (i.e. “spam”, “nsfw”). This is a separate service, so they do not have to run a PDS (personal data server) or a client app in order to do so.

  • Labels can be automatically generated (by third-party services or by custom algorithms) or manually generated (by admins or by users themselves)

  • Any service or person in the network can choose how these labels get used to determine the final user experience.

Everybody gets to run their own personal social media with their own content decisions. And all of us get to take action against hatred as we see fit. Humor5 can be standard. No trolls can be standard. Our behavior has consequences.6

This is an email from leadership at Bluesky explaining the limits to a user:

In order to stick the landing on this article, I had a conversation on bluesky with an AI duck. I'm just gonna post the screenshot of that because I think it makes my point better than any additional writing would, and it answers the concerns AOC raised in the earlier Skeet about how this can safely move forward.

and then….

and then…

the ducks get it7.

Who is with me? We can create faster than you can hate.

By the way, I already wrote two physical books…

…that exist in the world—of poetry!—on the topic. That's how fast this thing moves.

I’m not saying it’s good poetry. I am saying it exists faster than you imagined. And creativity will protect us from haters.

—Owen Scott Muir, M.D.

(^link to Amazon author store).

Subscribing to this newsletter is going to keep you up-to-date with all of the happenings that matter.

1

You can follow this guide to download it! Without an invite code, it won’t help. I am on BlueSky social. I am reporting from the inside. No, I don’t have an invite code.

2

For the record, AOC will be president. She is freaking brilliant. Has the skill set to hold her own. This is not a political comment, but watching her operate, I just want to say for the record: This Will Happen.

3

For several days on blue sky come on people have been going back and forth about what call posts. A bunch of dumb names were used. Memes were made. Bloot. Sleet. Skeet. Blust. Skeet has a slang definition that—ahem—has the most ontological relationship with urology as a medical discipline.

4

Humor involves anticipating someone else's thoughts and surprising them. When two people find the same thing funny, it signifies a mutual understanding and connection. This is in stark contrast to hateful or abusive interactions, where a joke may only be amusing to one person involved.

5

This is the future where people who like to make fun of each other get to do so. And people who don't like that don't. And nobody but you get to decide what you like. It’s so much more when scaled with AI thought because humor and shitposting are magic.

6

This is a familiar structure awesome. It's how we handle in-person interactions. We apply filters in our brains: If you've ever heard somebody say: “don't bring that shit in here!”—you just got to experience compostable moderation in real-time. The filter of that person or that space lets them identify your comment as something that has a conceptual tag, and the community member informs you of the policy.

7

My typos are clearly a strategy to allow for AI identification of the fact that I’m human and not a terrible speller.
